thread:
oana: quick heads-up: onboarding run for new quant-lite model (qlite-v1-int8) is showing occasional malformed funcall outputs during streaming toolcalls. low rate (~0.18%) but reproducible under stress. anyone else hit this with streaming+funcalls?

ravi: can you paste a raw snippet and the exact runtime flags?

maria: also add which serializer (ndjson vs single-chunk) and whether we used prefix_kv.

oana: runtime=staging-dedicated, model=qlite-v1-int8, streaming=true, funcalls=true, serializer=ndjson, kv_prefixing=enabled. sample below from captured failed stream: 

oana: ```
{"tool":"lookup","args":{"id":"abc123"}}

\xf0\x9f\x98\x80\x00

{"tool":"confirm","args":{"ok":true}}
```

dex: heh, emoji bytes followed by a NUL. looks like multibyte utf8 followed by zero padding. are these zero bytes only when we switch microbatch or when switching model variants?

oana: we only saw it with qlite-v1-int8 as primary. running a fallback (qlite-fp16) eliminates the failure in replay.

ravi: ops-bot: dump parse_failures for qlite-v1-int8 (last 24h) split by serializer and streaming flag

ops-bot: Metrics (model=qlite-v1-int8, 24h):
- total reqs: 120,890
- parse_failures: 221 (0.18%)
- streaming=true & serializer=ndjson: 86% of failures
- streaming=false: 6% of failures
- kv_prefixing enabled in 74% of failing requests

maria: strong signal for streaming+ndjson. two quick hypotheses: (1) encoder emits multi-byte utf sequences split across chunk boundaries and a zero pad appears when a buffer is recycled; (2) our ndjson framing logic doesn't guard against zero-length chunks and emits \x00 bytes.

dex: low-effort mitigations: (A) post-decode sanitizer replace(/[^\x09\x0A\x0D\x20-\xFF]/g,'') but that mask is lossy; (B) strip \x00 bytes only; (C) fast retry with non-streaming mode for structured outputs on first failure.

oana: i'll avoid broad sanitizer that masks high-bit bytes since emojis are valid. prefer stripping only \x00 and invalid utf sequences. also we'll try a fast non-streaming retry for structured toolcalls (1 attempt).

ravi: triage plan:
1) reproduce with harness forcing chunk splits inside multibyte characters (seq_len=850, batch=10, streaming chunk size small)
2) capture per-chunk raw hex + token-id sequences for failed cases
3) run with kv_prefixing off and with fallback pinned to fp16 to confirm model-specificity
4) try runtime zero-fill of microbatch tails before dequant to see if that removes NULs

maria: I'll grep runtime commits for any recent changes to the ndjson streamer; there was an optimization two weeks ago that preallocates buffers and reuses them. could be use-after-free style corruption if not cleared. filing infra ticket INF-331.

oana: added quick capture hook now (logs token_ids and per-chunk hex for parse_fail events). rolling canary rule: route sequences >768 to qlite-fp16 for now.

dex: local replay with simple sanitizer (remove-only-null bytes) reduced failures from 58 -> 5 in a 1h replay. remaining 5 look like truncated multibyte sequences (decoder produced U+FFFD).

ravi: that suggests both zero-pad and true truncation. if truncation, it might be chunking semantics in ndjson framing. add chunk checksum at streamer boundary so we can detect chunk reordering/truncation.

maria: good idea. also run a test where we disable buffer reuse in that ndjson path to see if it affects failure rate.

oana: next steps and owners: oana (repro capture + sanitizer eval), mari a (ndjson buffer reuse grep + INF-331), ravi (checksum instrumentation + routing pin), dex (quick runtime zero-fill experiment in staging).

ops-bot: Update: routing pin applied. monitoring parse_failures. current canary sample (45m): failures 45 -> 9 after pin and null-strip sanitizer.

dex: if zero-fill removes the remainder, we can schedule a small runtime patch. otherwise need deeper memory-safety audit in ndjson streamer.

oana: will post captured artifacts shortly. thanks all. leaving thread open until kernel/streamer root cause confirmed. :mag:

ops-bot: note: created alert ML-STREAM-12 to trigger if parse_failures >0.1% for qlite-v1-int8 in prod routing.
